clue.text: Chapter on tract in a wild southern region

indicators.note: on here means placed after, so the chapter letter is attached at the end
wild means out of control, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chapter of a travel book on an untamed tract in the far south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges TRACT + IN + A into ANTARCTI; 'on' adds C at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The polar continent and its surrounding seas make up the southernmost zone of the globe.

clue.text: Maiden in island turned up for leisurely walk

indicators.note: in tells us the maiden letter sits inside the island word
in a down clue, turned up means the island's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A girl on an island who has popped up for a gentle stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' turns ELBA into ABLE; 'in' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To saunter is to move at an easy, unhurried pace on foot.

clue.text: Bad luck, Head showing such intractability

parts.note: 'Tough!' is said as a curt comment on someone's misfortune
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness place names

explanation.surface: A head teacher showing stubbornness and offering only 'bad luck' to complainers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a person in charge; here it is a promontory, NESS. 'such' points back to the tough, hard quality the pieces describe.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubbornness, hardness and resistance to being managed are all senses of the noun.

clue.text: Advert and article about purpose of plebiscites

parts.note: to advert to something is to refer to it, an old-fashioned verb
an end is an aim or purpose
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An advertisement and a newspaper article about the purpose of public votes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advert' looks like a noun for an advertisement but is the verb meaning refer. 'about' here simply joins article to purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural Latin form for national votes put directly to the electorate on a single question.

clue.text: Admit defeat and include the dryer for no extra charge

definitions.meaning: to concede and give up, from a boxer's corner signalling surrender

definitions.text: include the dryer for no extra charge
definitions.meaning: to throw something in is to add it free, and the dryer here is a bath sheet

explanation.surface: A shop owner caves in to a haggler and gives away a bath sheet for free.
explanation.definitionFit: The boxing idiom for surrender also reads literally as tossing in a drying cloth as a freebie.

clue.text: One choir remains discordant, whatever happens

indicators.note: discordant means out of harmony, so the singers' words are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Only one choir is left in a singing contest, and it sings out of tune regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means regardless of the weather or circumstances, no matter what.

clue.text: Half-heartedly shuffle plunder

indicators.note: the heart of the shuffle word is a doubled letter, and losing half of that pair leaves one

parts.note: to riffle cards is to shuffle them by flicking the edges together

explanation.surface: Someone shuffles cards listlessly while planning a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: RIFFLE has FF at its centre; 'Half-heartedly' drops one F.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack or loot a place is to search through it and steal.

clue.text: Head of bank leaves local office for farm

indicators.note: leaves means goes away from, so the letter is removed from the office word

parts.note: a branch is a local office of a bank or firm

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bank manager quits the local branch to go farming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of bank' is B; taking it from BRANCH leaves the farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A large North American livestock estate, especially for cattle.

clue.text: Shawl originally found in central Manchuria

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of each of the two words
central picks the middle three letters of the place name

explanation.surface: A shawl that first turned up in the heart of Manchuria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives F and I, the first letters of 'found in'; 'central' takes the middle CHU from Manchuria.
explanation.definitionFit: A small triangular lace scarf worn over the shoulders, a type of wrap.

clue.text: Beg honoured companion to go in for the high jump?

indicators.note: to go in tells us the honoured companion is placed inside the begging word

parts.note: to entreat is to beg or plead
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Someone pleads with a distinguished colleague to enter the high jump at sports day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the high jump' suggests athletics or punishment; it is a ballet leap. The question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballet leap in which the dancer crosses the feet rapidly in mid-air.

clue.text: One deliberately deceiving old man about pound

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the old man's word wraps round the pound letter

parts.note: an old buffer is a fuddy-duddy old man
L stands for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A conman tries to trick an elderly man out of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker player or bluster who pretends to hold more than they do.

clue.text: Peel's queen, perhaps

parts.note: Peel is a town on the Isle of Man and a queen is a female cat, so this is a tailless island feline

explanation.surface: A question about the royal consort of a statesman named Peel.
explanation.walkthrough: Peel suggests Sir Robert Peel the prime minister; it is the Manx town, and queen is a mother cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailless breed of domestic cat from the Isle of Man, where Peel lies.

clue.text: Place near London where she resides? Not entirely

indicators.note: Not entirely means only part of the phrase is used, so the answer is a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: Asking whether a woman lives in some spot near the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across wherE SHE Resides.
explanation.definitionFit: A Surrey town in the commuter belt south-west of the capital.

clue.text: Plenty of storage space here in Herts home

parts.note: Ware is a town in Hertfordshire, the county north of London
a house is a home

explanation.surface: An estate agent praises the ample cupboards in a Hertfordshire house.
explanation.definitionFit: A large building for holding goods before sale or distribution.

clue.text: Serious novelist, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means we use how the writer's name is said, not spelt

parts.note: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy

explanation.surface: A remark that a novelist seems a grave fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave, severe and unsmiling in manner.

clue.text: Sheep he's left on farmland apt to be cut off

indicators.note: left means departed, so the letters H and E go from the sheep word

parts.note: he's reads as he has, and the word he supplies the letters removed
arable land is ploughed farmland

explanation.surface: A farmer's sheep have strayed from his field and risk being cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: SHEEP without HE leaves SEP; then add ARABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Able to be detached or separated from the rest.

clue.text: Handy cleaners may have it at their finger-tips

definitions.text: Handy cleaners may have it at their finger-tips

parts.words: Handy cleaners may have it at their finger-tips
parts.note: handy means for the hands, and the cleaning tool works at the very ends of the fingers

explanation.surface: Domestic cleaners always keep their kit close to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handy cleaners' sounds like skilful charladies; it means things that clean hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A small stiff brush for scrubbing under the fingernails.

clue.text: As a performer, she may be winning on points

definitions.text: As a performer, she may be winning on points

parts.words: As a performer, she may be winning on points
parts.note: a dancer performs on the points of her toes, while winning on points is a boxing phrase

explanation.surface: A female boxer's performance earns a points victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winning on points' suggests a boxing decision; a ballet dancer works on the tips of her toes.
explanation.definitionFit: A female classical dancer, who dances en pointe.

clue.text: Girl taking the female inside to draw

indicators.note: inside tells us the female word goes within the girl's name

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
she is the female pronoun
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl brings another woman in to sit for a drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw' suggests sketching; here it means pulling a blade from its scabbard. 'inside' puts the female within the girl, and 'taking' tacks the article on.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a sword is to pull it from its scabbard.

clue.text: Nutty flavour, to one chap, is awful

indicators.note: awful means dreadful, so the letters before it are mangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man finds a certain ice-cream flavour terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: A green nut used to flavour ice cream and sweets.

clue.text: Composer making record for audience

indicators.note: for audience means the word is meant to be heard rather than read

parts.note: a list is a written record

explanation.surface: A composer making a recording for listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian pianist and writer of music.

clue.text: Considers drink — tisane, possibly

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink

indicators.note: possibly means the herbal word might be rearranged into something else

parts.note: the fodder letters, a herbal tea

explanation.surface: Weighing up whether to have a drink, perhaps a herbal tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder or mull something over, like a cow chewing cud.

clue.text: Sound style for a country house

indicators.note: Sound means we hear the next word, not spell it

parts.note: manner is style or way

explanation.surface: Sound style choices for a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable; it signals a word said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A landed estate's principal residence, a grand rural home.

clue.text: Unpleasant name given to a place of debauchery

parts.note: a sty is a filthy or depraved place, figuratively a den of vice

explanation.surface: A place of vice gets a nasty reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Disagreeable, horrid or offensive.

clue.text: Employees retained by press chief to edit

indicators.note: retained by means held inside, so the workers go within the editor's abbreviation

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the chief at a newspaper
men are workers or employees

explanation.surface: Newspaper staff are kept on by the editor to correct copy.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct and improve a text by revising it.

clue.text: Gambled, securing diamonds, diamonds, and more diamonds

parts.note: D is the card abbreviation for diamonds
ice is slang for diamonds
D again for the card suit, with more meaning another lot

explanation.surface: A gambler won a hoard of diamonds at the tables.
explanation.walkthrough: Diamonds appear three times, as D, as slang ICE, and as D again; 'securing' joins them as winnings.
explanation.definitionFit: To dice is to play with dice, so the past tense means gambled.

clue.text: Cutter observed by crew

indicators.note: by means next to, placing the seen word beside the crew word

parts.note: a band is a group or crew
saw is the past tense of see, meaning observed

explanation.surface: A cutting tool watched by the workmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A power tool with an endless toothed blade for cutting wood or metal.

clue.text: Stupid description of Dostoyevsky's hero

definitions.meaning: Prince Myshkin is the title character of The Idiot, so an adjective for him

explanation.surface: Calling the Russian novelist's protagonist a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolish behaviour, like that of the simpleton in the Russian novel.

clue.text: See about artillery's retreat in good time

indicators.note: about means around, so the bishop's seat wraps round the gunners

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see

indicators.note: retreat means go back, so the artillery letters are read backwards

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: Watching the gun crews pull back in good order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a bishop's diocese, not a verb. 'retreat' turns the artillery letters back to front before 'about' wraps the cathedral city round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Before the expected or appointed time, punctual.

clue.text: Besides pork pies, a loaf is in store

parts.note: rhyming slang: pork pies means lies, untruths
rhyming slang: loaf of bread means head

explanation.surface: Besides pork pies, there's a loaf for sale in the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are Cockney rhyming slang: 'pork pies' are lies, 'loaf (of bread)' is the head. 'Besides' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Awaits in the future, about to happen.
